source_documents.title: From live cells to real-world samples: A PET-based ultrafast and photostable turn-on fluorescent probe for on-site quantification and in vivo visualization of HClO

reference_evidence_units.quote: By utilizing photoinduced electron transfer (PET) quenching, it exhibits an extremely low background signal.
reference_evidence_units.subject: CUM-DMTC

reference_evidence_units.quote: In the intact probe, the energy of the HOMO localized on the fluorophore is lower than that of the donorcentered HOMO, enabling spontaneous electron transfer from the donor to the photoexcited fluorophore.
reference_evidence_units.subject: CUM-DMTC
reference_evidence_units.statement: Thiocarbamate donor HOMO above the coumarin HOMO.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This thermodynamically favorable PET pathway efficiently quenches the fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: CUM-DMTC

reference_evidence_units.quote: Meanwhile, upon reaction with HClO, the fluorescence quantum yield of the probe increased from 3.57% to 50.75%, representing a more than 14-fold enhancement.
reference_evidence_units.subject: CUM-DMTC + HClO

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Paper's explanation of the low background (QY 3.57%): PET from the thiocarbamate to the excited coumarin (DFT).
